query: Everything on One Hand {The room has gone quiet. Players from every other table have drifted over to stand around yours. Grisk takes off his rings, one by one, and sets them on the pot. "Everything," he says. "One hand. Then we see who goes home."|Grisk deals this one himself. Nobody has done that in years, someone whispers.|The whole back room is standing around your table now. Grisk rolls up his velvet sleeves.} Whatever is in the pot tonight is in it again, and more besides. Everything on one hand {Grisk turns his last card, looks at yours, and starts to laugh. He puts his rings back on, one by one, and pushes the pot to you. "Don't come back for a month," he says. "I mean it kindly."|You win, and the back room applauds. By morning the village has three versions of the story, and in all of them you are taller.|The whole room breathes out at once. Grisk shakes your hand with both of his. "A real player," he says, and it sounds like a warning.} {Grisk turns a card you didn't think was left in the deck. Everything you won tonight goes back to him, and then some. He's very kind about it, which is worse.|You lose it all on one card. The crowd drifts back to their own tables as if nothing happened. On the stair, a prefect's lamp is waiting.|The pot goes to Grisk. He counts it slowly, in front of you, and offers to call you a carriage. There are no carriages.} Leave on a winning streak {You stand up in the middle of the hush. "Another night," you say, and leave with two pots in your coat. Grisk applauds, alone, and then everyone does.|You refuse the last hand. The back room is torn between booing and admiration. Your purse settles it.|"Not tonight," you say. Grisk grins all his teeth. "That," he says, "is how you get to play again."}

results.title: Let It Ride
results.excerpt:
Let It Ride
{Grisk sweeps your winnings into one neat stack and pushes it back into the middle of the table. "Let it ride," he says. "The second hand pays double. Most people stop here. Most people are dull."|Grisk is already shuffling. "Again?" he says, as if it were your idea.
